key_insight: A variational adiabatic eigensolver can prepare high-fidelity excited states for silicon band-structure calculations on NISQ hardware.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical quantum workflow for estimating semiconductor electronic structure with fewer qubits and better excited-state handling than standard approaches.
method: Use momentum-space truncation to reduce the silicon problem to a modest qubit register.
Combine adiabatic evolution with variational optimization in a phase-based loss function.
Run multi-qubit parameterized circuits on a superconducting quantum processor to prepare valence and conduction eigenstates.
evidence_signal: Experiments achieved over 96% single-shot state fidelity, with measured energies within 0.5 eV of theory and refined errors below 0.01 eV after oscillation fitting.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate circuit calibration and readout quality, so noise and hardware drift may limit scalability beyond the demonstrated system.
paper_title: Electronic Band Structure of Silicon Determined via a Variational Adiabatic Eigensolver: Theory and Experiment
